lotl.body: The Leafs beat the Islanders 4-2, moving to 9-14 on the season. They sit 12th in eastern conference, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Blue Jackets 3-4. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: at Bruins on Fri 11/27 at 1:00 PM ET. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason's first heavyweight swing ended with Toronto missing - and now the club must prove it had a plan beyond Tarik Skubal. The Blue Jays reportedly offered the left-hander nine years and $420 million before the Mets claimed him for $450 million, a bruising loss but also a clear sign that this front office is willing to spend at the top of the market. The next move matters more than the missed one. Dylan Cease, José Soriano and Trey Yesavage give Toronto a credible core, while Cody Ponce and Spencer Arrighetti remain in the mix; Freddy Peralta has emerged as the obvious alternative. But the greater repair may belong in the lineup, which scored the fewest runs in the Majors last season. Andrés Giménez's viral statue is comic relief. Watch whether Toronto turns its Skubal money toward Peralta - and finally buys the offense this roster needs before March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A winnable night became another weight around Toronto's ankles. The Raptors fell 116-111 to Milwaukee on Monday, handing the Bucks their first win after 13 straight losses - a bruising reminder that Toronto's margin for error is paper-thin. At 6-11, fourth in the Atlantic and 7.5 games behind, this is not contender form; the minus-2.5 scoring margin tells the same story in quieter language. Tyler Herro's 32 points drove Milwaukee's comeback, while Toronto again lacked RJ Barrett, sidelined by a right hamstring strain. Collin Murray-Boyles did return from concussion protocol, but his late miss, followed by Ja'Kobe Walter's, left the Raptors staring at a squandered chance to build momentum. One loss is not a crisis. This trajectory is. Friday's 7:30 p.m. meeting with Brooklyn is the next test - and a chance to prove Toronto can finish close games before the season drifts away.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Washington has found a pulse, and it is beating through Jayden Daniels. The Commanders stunned Cincinnati 22-20 Monday night, surviving a finish that left the Bengals howling about two seconds that should have remained on the clock after Washington's go-ahead field goal. Daniels answered the noise the only way that matters: by throwing. With the game tightening, he hit rookie Antonio Williams for gains of 22 and 42 yards, driving Washington 64 yards in 34 seconds before Drew Stevens delivered the winner. The victory moves the Commanders to 4-5-1, second in the NFC East, two games behind, and riding a two-game winning streak. This is no juggernaut, but it is a team discovering late-game nerve - and a quarterback willing to seize the wheel. Next comes Sunday's 4:25 p.m. visit to Arizona, where Washington must prove this surge travels.

article.title: Leafs Beat Islanders to End Nine-Game Skid
paragraphs: The Leafs finally have a win to carry into the holiday week, rallying past the Islanders 4-2 on Monday. Gavin McKenna scored the go-ahead goal, while Easton Cowan, Dakota Joshua and Chris Tanev also scored. Anthony Stolarz stopped 20 shots. Toronto, now 9-14 and 12th in the Eastern Conference, visits Boston on Friday at 1:00 p.m. ET on TSN.

The Raptors lost a winnable one to Milwaukee, 116-111, despite Scottie Barnes scoring 31 points and adding eight assists. Jakob Poeltl grabbed 10 rebounds. Toronto faces Brooklyn on Friday at 7:30 p.m. The Commanders, meanwhile, beat Cincinnati 22-20 after Jayden Daniels threw for 289 yards and ran for 55, with Antonio Williams catching 122 yards. Washington visits Arizona Sunday at 4:25 p.m. on Fox.
The Jays have no game until their March 25 regular-season opener at Yankee Stadium, scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. The rotation remains the offseason focus, with potential additions ahead.
